purpose: Development-only audit of stage-boundary option value after the frozen v1 policy would stop at challenger compile index 65. Test whether FINISH_STAGE1 is a meaningful compute action even when no challenger endpoint yet beats the retained incumbent, because stage completion may unlock a second local-search stage. This v0 audit does not fit or tune a policy.
search_contract: Identical frozen local-search substrate used by the preceding challenger studies: construct verified two-arm incumbent from natural/RCM starts; construct an independent seeded start; ROBDD objective is reachable live nodes; relocation neighborhood moves one variable; candidates require vertex-separation width <= current_width + 1; a stage evaluates the complete legal relocation neighborhood before accepting only a strict live-node improvement; at most two accepted moves; every challenger BDD candidate compilation is charged; cross-order Hamming-rank oracle plus endpoint-local exhaustive truth oracle.

frozen_v1_reference.first_decision: Evaluate through challenger compile index min(H,65). If a verified endpoint already beats the incumbent, v1 finishes the challenger. Otherwise, when best_gap65 > 11 v1 stops with the incumbent; when best_gap65 <= 11 v1 continues.
frozen_v1_reference.audit_population: Only states where v1 would stop at index 65: challenger remains, no certificate has appeared, and best_gap65 > 11. These states receive full counterfactual tail audit with development propensity 1.0. Other cases are recorded for denominator/context but are not used as stop-region option-value examples.

stage_aware_action_semantics.STOP: Return the retained two-arm incumbent with zero additional challenger work after index 65.
stage_aware_action_semantics.FINISH_STAGE1: Pay exactly the remaining legal BDD compilations needed to complete the current relocation neighborhood and decide whether a strict seeded self-improvement exists. This may have zero immediate incumbent reward but can create a gateway order from which stage 2 becomes legal.
stage_aware_action_semantics.SEARCH_STAGE2: Legal only if stage 1 accepts a strict seeded self-improvement. Search the second relocation stage; for this v0 audit the full stage is observed so later sequential-prefix policies can be designed without selective labels.
stage_aware_action_semantics.OUTPUT_MERGE: Always return min(retained incumbent, best verified challenger endpoint witnessed so far); therefore experimental challenger work cannot worsen final live-node quality relative to the incumbent.

gateway_positive_definition: exhaustive_gain > 0 AND stage1_immediate_incumbent_gain == 0 AND stage2_exists. This is descriptive option value: completing stage 1 unlocks a stage 2 that eventually beats the incumbent even though stage 1 itself does not.
co_primary_metrics: aggregate exhaustive gain arising from gateway-positive cases / total stop-region exhaustive gain
stage1 remaining compile cost distribution and fraction of full audited tail cost
family-specific exhaustive gain and gateway-positive rate, with watts/erdos reported separately
per-case no-harm invariant from retained incumbent merge
mechanism_hypothesis: If most valuable stop-region cases are gateway-positive, arbitrary small fixed prefixes and immediate certificate reward are misaligned. The next controller should price stage completion as an option-purchase action and learn future value conditional on an unlock, rather than require immediate incumbent improvement.
no_use_for_confirmation: 914xxx/915xxx prior v2 confirmation remains frozen confirmation evidence and is never used to fit a future stage-aware policy
future_policy_rule: Any learned stage-aware policy must be specified in a new preregistered protocol after this audit. It must use a wholly new confirmation split after fitting. No threshold, budget, lambda, or action cutoff may be selected on future confirmation outcomes.
scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD variable-order search only. Stage-aware conclusions are mechanism evidence for compute allocation, not a theorem-proving performance result.
